newsitem.title: USA: Milosevic to free up media for elections.
newsitem.headline: Milosevic to free up media for elections.

text.p: Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic will allow opposition politicians access to state-controlled television and radio for elections set for later this year, Serbia's information minister said on Monday.

The minister, Radmila Milentijevic, told reporters at the National Press Club that Milosevic was planning to allow greater freedoms for Serbia's media, bowing to a key demand of opposition candidates.
Asked if this meant that opponents of Milosevic would be allowed to appear on state-controlled television stations, Milentijevic replied: "Absolutely."
She said that the Milosevic government was "in the process of reform ... we want to find the most liberal law that governs the press in Western Europe and use it to model our regulations."

Milentijevic, who has dual American and Serbian citizenship and divides her time between New York and Belgrade, said she took her post earlier this month because "I am convinced that President Milosevic is determined to steer Yugoslavia toward democratization."
Serbia's opposition coalition, the three-party Zajedno (Together), took control of the Belgrade city council last week.

Though socialists still control both the Serbian and Yugoslav governments, Zajedno forced Milosevic's socialists to recognise local election results by staging daily street protests, which involved up to half a million people at their peak.

Zajedno's leaders said they want Milosevic's authoritarian government to free up the country's heavily controlled media and create fair conditions for parliamentary and presidential elections due later this year.
